How does SCRIPE v4.0 unify Sovereign REST Endpoints, Principal Permanence, 4-Tier Dynamic Workflow Evaluation, and 12-Port Directed Studio Wiring?

Long image

A

Answer

SCRIPE v4.0 eliminates colloquial first-person REST routes, repairs session refresh RBAC wiping, enforces a strict 4-tier dynamic workflow graph evaluator with zero hardcoded stage keys or linear sortOrder assumptions, locks all 12 React Flow Studio handles as directed sources with card-body drop resolution, upgrades Kanban drag-and-drop to zero-offset DragOverlay portals, and restructures 360 views under strict <= 300-line and 100% EN/AR parity invariants.1

  1. All 12 first-person me / my / myTenant endpoint groups standardize on third-person, kebab-case sovereign REST naming (/principal, /current, /current-tenant, /effective, /navigation, /self-service) enforced in CI by endpoint-casing-contract.test.ts.1
  2. GET /api/v1/auth/admin/principal and RefreshTokenCommandHandler re-prime _permissionCache.PrimeCache while use-auth-refresh.ts defensively preserves roles and permissions.2
  3. Both UniversalWorkflowEngine and evaluateWorkflowTransition execute strict 4-tier precedence without hardcoded stage-key hijacks or sortOrder-based rollback traps, computing allowed_instant vs. allowed_screen_required vs. blocked dynamically.3
  4. CrmStageFlowHandles, useCrmWorkflowCanvasGraph, and crmWorkflowStudioMappers lock all 12 interactive ports to type="source", capture connectOriginRef, resolve card-body drops via onConnectEnd, and preserve entity-scoped promptFields and allowInboundFromAny.4

1

How does the Sovereign Enterprise Endpoint Naming Overhaul eliminate 404 drift and first-person routes?

ASP.NET Core registers SlugifyParameterTransformer globally so every [controller] route token renders as lowercase kebab-case (for example UserGroupsController becomes /api/v1/user-groups), whereas ASP.NET route matching is case-insensitive only on exact hyphen placement.1 Colloquial first-person segments (/me, /my*, myTenant, createForMyTenant, myChildren, my-tenant) and un-hyphenated PascalCase segments (UserGroups) caused client/server contract drift. SCRIPE v4.0 replaces first-person routes with a third-person Sovereign Enterprise Principal vocabulary (/principal, /effective, /navigation, /current, /current-tenant, /self-service, /sudo-verify — eliminating colloquial /me and /my-* naming in favor of explicit scope nouns) across all 12 domain endpoint groups and pins the frontend endpoint registry in CI.

Contract Allowlist & Middleware Enforcement

endpoint-casing-contract.test.ts retains only one documented allowlist entry (ThemeBundles) for a not-yet-implemented backend controller so missing features remain explicit. On the backend, MustChangePasswordMiddleware explicitly whitelists ^/api/v\d+/auth/admin/principal$ alongside change-password, refresh, logout, and revoke while blocking all other routes with 403 until password rotation finishes.

How does Principal Session Refresh guarantee RBAC permanence across token rotations?

Diagram structure
  • Guard & useAuthRefresh client
  • Zustand useAppStore store
  • AdminAuthController api
  • IAdminPermissionCache cache
  • Identity Repo & UoW db
  • client → api · GET /api/v1/account/dossier (missing Admin roles)
  • api → client · 200 OK Account Dossier without full Role/Permission graph
  • client → store · setAuth(user, perms, []) wipes client RBAC
  • client → api · GET /api/v1/auth/admin/principal (authRepository.getCurrentPrincipal)
  • api → db · GetCurrentPrincipalQueryHandler loads Admin + Roles
  • db → api · Admin entity with role assignments & tenant status
  • api → cache · _permissionCache.PrimeCache(adminId, roles, perms, restricted, scopes)
  • cache → api · 30s admin:principal IMemoryCache & PermCache Primed
  • api → client · 200 OK AdminResponse / AdminProfileDto (Roles + Permissions)
  • client → store · Guard !user.id; preserve roles & perms
  • client → api · POST /api/v1/auth/admin/refresh (RefreshToken)
  • api → db · CAS TryRevokeAsync + Rotate RefreshToken (reuse protection)
  • db → api · Token rotated + Admin entity loaded
  • api → cache · RefreshTokenCommandHandler calls _permissionCache.PrimeCache(...)
  • api → client · 200 OK TokenResponse (Lean JWT + embedded UserProfile)

Previously, frontend auth refresh called /account/dossier, whose account dossier payload lacked full administrative roles and inheritedPermissions arrays, resetting Zustand RBAC state (roles: []) and triggering spurious 403/navigation lockouts. SCRIPE v4.0 binds auth hydration exclusively to GET /api/v1/auth/admin/principal (AdminAuthController.GetCurrentPrincipal -> GetCurrentPrincipalQueryHandler, cached under admin:principal:{userId}:{tenantId} and whitelisted in MustChangePasswordMiddleware), re-primes _permissionCache.PrimeCache on both principal reads and token rotations, and preserves existing RBAC arrays in use-auth-refresh.ts.2

  1. Sovereign Principal Endpoint ↗

    useAuthRefresh and route-guard.tsx call authRepository.getCurrentPrincipal() (AUTH_CORE_ENDPOINTS.PRINCIPAL), whitelisted during mcp=true by MustChangePasswordMiddleware.

  2. Server Cache Re-Priming ↗

    GetCurrentPrincipalQueryHandler caches under admin:principal:{id}:{tenant} (invalidated by UpdateAccountDossierCommandHandler) and calls _permissionCache.PrimeCache(...) for full Permissions and RestrictedFields parity.

  3. Defensive Client Hydration ↗

    If !user?.id, setAuth is skipped so malformed responses never clear auth state; if fresh arrays are empty, use-auth-refresh.ts retains state.roles and state.permissions.

  4. Token Rotation with UserProfile ↗

    RefreshTokenCommandHandler executes conditional atomic revocation (revoking all sessions on token reuse), re-primes _permissionCache, and embeds fresh UserProfile in TokenResponse.

How do Kanban DragOverlay portals and Strict 4-Tier Dynamic Workflow Graph Evaluation work together?

Ancestor containers with CSS transform, filter, or overflow break @dnd-kit drag coordinates by shifting the floating card away from the pointer. Simultaneously, legacy stage transition checks contained hardcoded target stage-key hijacks (closed_won, discovery, Disqualified, Qualified), linear sortOrder assumptions that misclassified unconnected edges as "Rollback" or blocked * -> closed_lost wildcards from higher-order custom stages, catch-block dialog fallbacks on backend rejections, and intermediate SortOrder exit-gate checks that ignored configured graph skip edges. SCRIPE v4.0 isolates DragOverlay in document.body, enforces pure 4-tier workflow graph precedence with lossless PostgreSQL hydration (fetchPipelinesFromBackend), and drives Kanban drops and CrmWorkflowTransitionDialog strictly from dynamic evaluation.3

Diagram structure
  • KanbanCard UI card
  • PointerSensor (5px) sensor
  • pointerWithin Collision collision
  • body DragOverlay portal
  • KanbanStageColumn Slot column
  • 4-Tier Workflow Engine engine
  • card → sensor · pointer down
  • sensor → collision · track rect
  • collision → portal · 0px ghost
  • collision → column · hover slot
  • column → engine · evaluate

Cards strip native HTML5 draggable attributes so @dnd-kit owns every drag sequence, while onPointerDown stopPropagation() shields inner action buttons (Link Organization, Convert to Deal, and stage chevron steppers) from initiating accidental drags. During hover, KanbanStageColumn renders a dashed kanban-drop-slot-${stageKey} indicator (data-drop-status) driven solely by evaluateWorkflowTransition: Signal Lime (border-nx-accent bg-nx-accent-wash) for allowed_instant, Amber (border-warning/60 bg-warning/10) for allowed_screen_required, and Red (border-destructive/60 bg-destructive/10) for blocked — with backend catch handlers reverting optimistic moves cleanly instead of forcing popups.

Diagram structure
  • Column Drop drop
  • 4-Tier Precedence resolve
  • Explicit Backward rollback
  • Dynamic Fields check
  • Blocked Slot blocked
  • allowed_instant instant
  • Screen Modal modal
  • check → instant · ready
  • check → modal · input needed
  • drop → resolve · graph lookup
  • resolve → blocked · no edge
  • resolve → rollback · matched edge
  • rollback → blocked · locked or rule
  • rollback → check · permitted
  1. Strict 4-Tier Precedence ↗

    Evaluates Tier 1 Direct (from -> to), Tier 2 Outbound Wildcard (from -> *), Tier 3 Global Inbound (* -> to), Tier 4 Global Wildcard (* -> *) plus allowInboundFromAny; removes hardcoded stage-key hijacks in crmWorkflowEngine.ts, useOpportunityViewModelHelpers.ts, and useLeadWorkflowActions.ts.

  2. Order-Agnostic Rollback & Rules ↗

    Emits order-agnostic blocked copy (No transition is configured from ... to ...); checks isExplicitBackward so * -> lost / done / direction: "global" edges skip allowRollback locks even when custom stages carry higher sortOrder; enforces restrict.* and Buying Committee rules.

  3. Dynamic Field & Gate Evaluation ↗

    Frontend isFieldSatisfiedOnRecord and backend ApplyAndSnapshotStageGateFieldsAsync / MoveOpportunityStageCommandHandler.GateValidation.cs (hasConfiguredTransitions) validate partyId, estimatedAmount, targetCloseDate, solutionFitConfirmed, primaryContactRole, qualificationNotes, and lossReasonCode against configured target and active exit gates without scanning skipped intermediate SortOrder stages; WorkflowPipelineMapper.RulesParsing.cs and UniversalWorkflowEngine.ValidateTransition.cs evaluate financial forecast bounds independently.

  4. Dynamic Screen vs. Instant Commit ↗

    requiresScreen computes purely from unfulfilledFields, promptFields, promptForComment, requiresLossReason, requiresCloseNotes, requiresReopenReason, shouldTriggerDealConversion, and matchedTransitions.length > 1; CrmWorkflowTransitionDialog + deriveTransitionDialogFlags + CrmWorkflowTransitionDynamicFields render @core/ui/* fields dynamically and commit ready moves in 1 gesture.

Lossless PostgreSQL Catalog & Store Hydration

crmWorkflowInitialCatalog.ts aligns wf-deal-default transitions 1:1 with CrmPipelineSeedCatalog.DefaultTransitions.cs (9 canonical edges, zero phantom local-only transitions), crmWorkflowsStoreHelpers.ts strips hardcoded transition-ID promptForComment overrides while preserving empty parsed transitions arrays (hasParsedTransitionsArray), useCrmWorkflowsStore persists schema version: 3, and both useOpportunityLifecycleActions.ts and LeadsView.tsx invoke fetchPipelinesFromBackend() on mount so Kanban and 2D Studio always share live PostgreSQL graph state.

How does the 12-Port source-Locked Directed React Flow Studio prevent wire reversal?

In @xyflow/react running with ConnectionMode.Loose, perimeter handles declared with type="target" (previously top-1, bottom-1, bottom-2, and left-1..3 in CrmStageFlowHandles) caused React Flow to automatically swap params.source and params.target before invoking onConnect, opening Create Workflow Transition with inverted From status and To status (for example turning Solution Fit -> Discovery into Discovery -> Solution Fit). Meanwhile, storing wireDraftSource in React state forced initialNodes to re-render mid-drag, and dropping a wire anywhere onto a stage card body outside a 7px handle circle failed without an onConnectEnd pointer fallback.4

  • 12 target Anchors companions
  • connectOriginRef Ref originref
  • onConnect / End Drop connectend
  • Lossless Studio Mapper mapper
  • CRM Pipeline API api
  • ports → originref · onConnectStart
  • originref → connectend · enforce origin
  • companions → connectend · passive target
  • connectend → mapper · direction & ports
  • mapper → api · PUT pipeline graph

How do Deal, Lead, Account, and Contact 360 views achieve progressive disclosure under 300 lines?

CRM 360 entity pages suffered from monolithic vertical stacks, duplicate transition/conversion cards, missing quick actions, and noisy multi-currency badges. SCRIPE v4.0 refactors all four 360 entity workspaces into modular, @core/ui/tabs-organized views that stay strictly below the <= 300-line architecture ceiling, obey Nexus matte surface tokens (--nx-surface, border-nx-line, shadow-none), and achieve zero inline bilingual ternaries across 108 locale pairs (18,040 keys).5
